subject: Renewal pricing discussion: phased uplift, usage fallback & escrow
messages:
From: Ethan Li <ethan.li@cloudterra.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@cloudterra.com, megan.rojas@cloudterra.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal draft + capacity increase request

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick chat this morning. We're coming up on our annual renewal and want to lock in the next 12 months. A couple of key asks from procurement and engineering:

- Increase committed capacity by ~45% for model inference (spikes expected in Q3).
- We need a 6-month price hold on current unit rates for committed usage.
- For unanticipated overage beyond commits, procurement prefers a measured usage fallback (pay-as-you-go) instead of punitive overage rates.

Attached is our internal forecast and SLA expectations. Can Redwood put together a proposal that includes a staged commit (quarterly ramp), a limited credit buffer for Q3 spikes, and language for a usage fallback? Also cc'ing Megan from procurement to coordinate PO/timing.

Appreciate a proposal by EOD Friday so we can review with Finance next week.

—Ethan
CloudTerra, Head of ML Platforms

Attachment: CloudTerra_forecast_Q3-Q4.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Li <ethan.li@cloudterra.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, megan.rojas@cloudterra.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal draft + capacity increase request

Ethan — thanks for the context and the forecast. Quick read-through attached; below is a practical proposal we can review before formalizing: 

Summary proposal (high level):
- 12-month renewal with a phased commit: 25% of the requested uplift effective at renewal, then two equal quarterly increases to reach 100% uplift by month 6. This keeps your unit economics predictable during ramp.
- Price hold: 6-month price hold on committed unit rates starting at the contract effective date; then standard annual indexation thereafter.
- Credit buffer: one-time Q3 surge credit equal to 10% of the first-quarter uplift spend, available as bill credits to offset unexpected spikes.
- Usage fallback: for usage above the committed pool, bill at standard PAYG rates (no penalty multiplier). We can define a soft-threshold true-up cadence (monthly true-up) so spikes are reconciled quickly.
- Escrowed overage protection: Redwood can escrow an agreed credit amount (mutually acceptable) that releases only if monthly overage exceeds the credit in two consecutive months. This protects your cashflow while giving Redwood visibility.

Attachments: CloudTerra_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf (proposal), draft term language for escrow and true-up included.

Next steps: if that aligns, I can loop in Sales Ops for a clean PO/DocuSign flow and Legal for MA redlines. Ben, can you validate the credit accounting treatment (how credits apply across invoices)? Monica, can you pre-check capacity allocation feasibility on the Dedicated pool?

Thanks — available for a 30m call tomorrow afternoon if useful.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Direct: +1 415-555-0124

Jonas / Monica —

Reviewed the proposal. A few operational notes and a small ask from Finance (copied Marissa):

1) Credit accounting: the 10% Q3 surge credit should be applied line-item to the first invoice after the spike quarter closes; Finance prefers a single-line credit rather than distributed invoice adjustments to simplify reconciliation.
2) Escrow mechanics: Legal will want specific trigger language. Proposed clean approach: escrow is funded as a pre-pay credit (applied to invoices) and held on Redwood's ledger; if unused after 6 months it rolls forward as account credit unless specific misuse is identified. Marissa — can you draft the simple clause (2 paragraphs) and attach to the MA redlines?
3) Capacity feasibility: Monica confirms Dedicated pool can absorb ramp but requests a 48-hour lead time for any burst beyond 1.5x committed Q4 average. We need to bake that into the SLA appendix.

I suggest we combine these into a single proposal PDF and return to CloudTerra for an approval call. Jonas — if CloudTerra accepts, Sales Ops can originate the DocuSign envelope.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
